next_step: Run 48h p95/p99 latency soak test on dedicated staging pool; align measurement spec with infra
notes: Account summary: Verdant provides latency-sensitive trading tools (pre-trade and post-trade assistance). They're exploring Redwood Dedicated to guarantee tail-latencies during market-open spikes.

Primary asks: reserved GPU pools, explicit throughput guarantees for peak 09:30-10:30 ET windows, strict p99 SLOs for both streaming and non-streaming flows, and server-side & client-side measurement alignment to avoid SLA disputes.

Latency targets discussed on demo: non-streaming (complete response) target p50=50ms, p95=150ms, p99=300ms; streaming (first-token latency + per-token steady-state) target first-byte p50=30ms, p95=100ms, p99=250ms. They insist on explicit definition of 'first-byte' for streaming vs 'end-to-end' for non-streaming.

Measurement model notes: Verdant will perform client-side timing (browser/edge SDK) and expects Redwood to provide server-side metrics instrumented at the gateway + model host (ingest->first-byte, first-byte->last-byte). Need mapping doc: client-send->server-receive offset, network RTT adjustment, and clock-drift mitigation (NTP/SDK sync).

Streaming vs non-streaming alignment: SE recommends dual-SLO approach: publish both server-side p95 and client-observed p95. Contractual SLA will reference server-side p95 with a reconciliation window and sample-based client audits. Verdant prefers a 5% tolerance between client/server p95 during soak tests before final SLA language.

Reserved GPU planning: target baseline throughput = 600 rps sustained during market open; avg request size ~80 tokens (prompt+response), burst headroom x2 for 2-min spikes. Proposed Dedicated config: 8xA100 equivalent GPUs with autoscale burst option. Redwood to provide projected token cost and ops runbook for warmup strategy.

SLA negotiation topics: uptime target asked = 99.95% with credits, max allowable p99 degradation during scheduled maintenance, and definition of downtime for streaming sessions. Verdant legal flagged sample SLA clause for 'graceful degradation' and wants rollback policies for canary model upgrades.

POC plan: 1) Instrumentation spec doc (Redwood to deliver) 2) Staging deploy with traffic replay for two market-open windows (48h soak) 3) Compare server P50/P95/P99 vs client SDK numbers 4) Adjust batching/quantization and re-run 5) Final SLA language and reserved capacity sizing. Target POC start: 2026-03-15 (pending procurement).

Quotes / paraphrases: 'We can tolerate small variance but need deterministic tails on market open — a single bad p99 costs us millions in slippage.'; SE note: "Need to capture per-route token distribution to validate batching impact."

Security/regulatory: data residency for trade metadata must remain in us-east-1; KMS integration required for request logs. SOC2 report required prior to procurement sign-off. They requested retention controls for logs (90/365 day tiers).
Commercial: estimated ARR based on proposed reserved config $250k-$750k. Procurement asked for 12 month commit with quarterly performance reviews.
